title: A Learnable Meta World - Stop Signs

cards.note: In New South Wales, especially in Sydney, some stop signs have three big holes making it unique for this region.
Stop signs in Cambodia always have the word "Stop" written in Khmer (ឈប់) in addition to the English word.
Stop signs in New Brunswick always have the word "Stop" written in France (Arrêt) in addition to the English word.
Stop signs in Québec always have the word "Stop" written in France (Arrêt). Beware that "Arrêt" is also written on New Brunswick stop signs!
Costa Rica, Guatemala, Panama and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
Guatemala, Panama, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
Israel is the only country that uses a symbol on its stop signs, which makes it unique and easily recognizable.
Stop signs in Malaysia always have the word "Stop" written in Malay (Berhenti).
Mexico, Panama, Costa Rica and Guatemala are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
Panama, Guatemala, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.

The word "Pare" on stop signs is widely used in all of Latin America excluding Mexico, Panama, Costa Rica and Guatemala. That means you can spot it in Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia, Peru, Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic.
The edge of the stop signs in Singapore has a white square outline making it unique.
Stop signs in Thailand always have the word "Stop" written in Thai (หยุด).
Stop signs in Türkiye always have the word "Stop" written in Turkish (Dur).
